podcasts.name: Training Data
podcasts.title: A Model For Everyone: How Ronak From Trajectory Is Building Products For Continual Learning
podcasts.description: Today’s agents are stuck in what Ronak Malde calls “pseudo continual learning”: intelligent, but updated in offline batches, like a paper road map you can’t reroute mid-trip. Ronak, co-founder of Trajectory, explains why closing that loop is the next learning paradigm, and why training your own model, which used to take a dedicated research team, months of work and hundreds of millions in compute, is now something a company can do in a few clicks with their own data. He details two research bets they are making available to everyone with their product: 1) a variant of GRPO that removes the need for a simulated environment by learning from single real-world rollouts instead of 16 replays of the same task, and 1) a meta-grader that increased data efficiency by 100x. Ronak explains how Harvey trained a model six times cheaper than frontier, improving an open-source baseline by over 4x on Harvey's own legal benchmark. He defines the difference between continual learning and recursive self-improvement and predicts product builders will become gardeners, setting trellises for products that grow themselves. Hosted by Pat Grady and Lauren Reeder, Sequoia Capital 0:00 – Introduction 0:45 – Pseudo continual learning: paper maps vs Google Maps 2:48 – Do we need new architectures? Rich Sutton, David Silver, and the missing layer 4:33 – From a $100M consulting model to a product: lessons from SWE-1 at Windsurf 7:36 – Harvey: 6x cheaper than frontier, 4% to 18% on its own benchmark 8:55 – Why "Trajectory": the unit of work is a task, not a token 10:13 – The primitives of continual learning: traces, replayable environments, reward 12:56 – Group Size 1 and the meta-grader: training without an environment or a labeled reward 16:16 – The platform: train, eval and deploy in one click, and who it's for 18:58 – Rogo and intelligence density 20:14 – What's next: curiosity, and why continual learning beats RSI on alignment 24:19 – Research and product under one roof, and the product builder as gardener 27:26 – Why work at Trajectory, and the optimistic case: from 1% to 99% ]]>

podcasts.name: No Priors
podcasts.title: Tokenization, Agentic Trading, Harmonic: Robinhood's Mission to Expand Ownership with CEO Vlad Tenev
podcasts.description: What does it mean to build wealth as an individual investor in today’s society, especially as gains continue to get concentrated into smaller groups of VCs or institutional investors? Robinhood’s CEO and co-founder Vlad Tenev has a vision that can be summed up in one word: Ownership. In this episode, Sarah Guo chats with Vlad to get a closer look at how Robinhood has evolved from a simple app to buy stocks at zero commission into a global conglomerate that allows customers to own across a wide variety of surfaces and asset classes. Vlad explains how Robinhood is helping users extend ownership amidst the current economy and ongoing AI revolution through Trump accounts, tokenization of privates, and newer product offerings like Robinhood Chain, Agentic Trading, and Agentic Credit Card. He also talks about how his new mathematical superintelligence startup, Harmonic, is revolutionizing the field and how he hopes it will decentralize new discoveries and inventions. Vlad and Sarah also discuss how prediction markets could tie into the ownership conversation, whether financial infrastructure can be optimized to enable even higher volumes of high-frequency trading, and his advice for maintaining a level head when facing the vagaries of a changing financial market.   Sign up for new podcasts every week. Email feedback to show@no-priors.com Follow us on Twitter: @NoPriorsPod | @Saranormous | @EladGil | @vladtenev | @RobinhoodApp | @HarmonicMath  Chapters:  00:46 – Intro to Vlad Tenev, His Background, and Robinhood Today 12:25 – A Revolutionary Future for Mathematics 18:49 – Robinhood’s Vision for Tokenization 26:06 – Monetizing Knowledge via Prediction Markets 28:48 – Impacts of Agentic Trading and Democratizing Trading 33:48 – Safeguarding Financial Infrastructure for a New Load of HFTs 38:30 – Ownership of Private Companies in the AI Revolution 48:34 – Robinhood and Trump Accounts  50:47 – Keeping a Steady Hand and Head as a Leader 53:48 – Conclusion ]]>

podcasts.name: Unsupervised Learning
podcasts.title: Ep 97: Jev Creator on Decision Models, Benchmark Fatigue & Why the Labs Missed It
podcasts.description: Jev creator and TypeSafe AI co-founder, Diogo Almeida, joins Jacob Effron to talk about why AI still isn't automating the easy work it's been smart enough to do for years, and why he built a new class of model around reliability. Diogo coauthored OpenAI's InstructGPT paper and spent two years in stealth building Jev, a "system one" model that returns structured decisions instead of text, which launched in September. Diogo and Jacob discuss what the viral launch was really like, why he thought Jev would take a week and it took years, why almost every LLM call should be meant for a machine, and why developers should push model providers harder on jaggedness. They also cover the tyranny of the KV cache in coding agents, why new model shapes are cheap and reliability is the hard part, his estimate that coding agents deliver a 20 to 40% speedup, why he sees financial engineering as the labs' underrated strength, and why he thinks we're two gigantic breakthroughs from true AI agency.   (0:00) Intro (1:14) The Early Bet on RLCD (4:40) Built for Humans vs Computers (6:39) Roadmap & Model Limitations (11:04) Mental Models of Models (16:07) Do LLMs Have a Place in 10 Years? (17:32) New Model Shapes (21:24) Problems Still Unsolved (27:00) The Tyranny of the KV Cache (31:21) Rethinking Coding Agents (34:40) Multimodality (37:52) Images, Games & Computer Use (39:36) Could This Have Been Built 5 Years Ago? (42:01) Benchmarks & Copycat Releases (44:12) Fundraising (45:27) Quickfire   OpenAI's InstructGPT paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.02155   Jacob is an AI investor at Redpoint Ventures. He's led Redpoint's investments in companies like Abridge, Physical Intelligence & Legora. Follow Jacob on Twitter (@jacobeffron). On Unsupervised Learning we probe the sharpest minds in AI in search for the truth about what's real today, what will be real in the future and what it all means for businesses and the world. If you're a builder, researcher or investor navigating the AI world, this podcast will help you deconstruct and understand the most important breakthroughs and see a clearer picture of reality. Subscribe to this show to stay up to date on our latest episodes.

podcasts.name: AI & I by Every
podcasts.title: The Inside Story of the 50 Who Built Modern AI With Kevin Roose
podcasts.description: How did the race to build AGI really unfold, and who made the decisions that shaped it? Tech journalist Kevin Roose interviewed 150 people at the center of the AI industry to find out. The result is The AGI Chronicles , a riveting account of  how modern AI was built and the choices that will determine what comes next.  On this week’s episode of The Every Podcast , Natalia Quintero sits down with Roose to talk about how he got a secretive industry to open up, how he did (and didn’t) use AI in his book writing process, and why he sees his job as explaining the “very confusing and insular” world of Silicon Valley to everyone else.
